exactPassages: Sidewalk cafes provided beyond the building line shall comply with the requirements of this section, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and with the projection limitations of Chapter 32 of this code.
No part of any awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment or removable platform of a sidewalk cafe shall be located:
2. So as to obstruct any exit from a building;
3. So as to obstruct any cellar access hatch or areaway;

Exception: Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, to cover a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.
Sidewalk cafes and access thereto shall comply with Chapter 11.

Where dining surfaces for the consumption of food or drink are provided, at least 10 percent of the total number of seating and standing spaces, but not less than one, of each type of dining surfaces shall be accessible and be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

Unless separated from seating inside the building by fire partitions complying with Section 713 , the seating for enclosed sidewalk cafes shall be added to that inside the building in order to determine whether a place of assembly certificate of operation is required.

testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, current agency authorization, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, or lawful seating capacity.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claim cannot be accepted from these passages. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with Section 3111, but also with the Zoning Resolution, the applicable requirements of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioners, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. More importantly, the café and its access must comply with Chapter 11. The supplied evidence contains no authorization-based waiver of that accessibility obligation.

The proposed furniture or equipment cannot obstruct the building exit, cellar access hatch, or areaway. A platform may cover a cellar entrance or areaway only if the commissioner permits it upon special application and it is easily removable, prominently designated, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, and covers an entrance or areaway not used as a required means of egress. The stated proximity to the exit and hatch does not itself establish an obstruction; the layout, clearances, and hatch use are not supplied.

Separate exterior seating is not automatically allowed for the place-of-assembly certificate-of-operation determination. If the sidewalk café is enclosed, its seating must be added to interior seating unless it is separated from the interior seating by fire partitions complying with Section 713. The selected provision does not state the seating-count treatment for a café that is not enclosed.

Accessibility also remains unresolved, not eliminated. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces must be accessible, with at least one accessible dining surface of each type; those surfaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level reached by an accessible route. The supplied seating totals, dining-surface types, accessible-surface distribution, and route information do not permit a compliance determination.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claim cannot be accepted from these passages. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with Section 3111, but also with the Zoning Resolution, the applicable requirements of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioners, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. More importantly, the café and its access must comply with Chapter 11. The supplied evidence contains no authorization-based waiver of that accessibility obligation.

supportedPoints.heading: Beyond-building-line cafés have additional compliance obligations
supportedPoints.explanation: A sidewalk café provided beyond the building line must comply with Section 3111, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations.

supportedPoints.heading: Café elements may not obstruct exits or cellar access
supportedPoints.explanation: No awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform of a sidewalk café may be located so as to obstruct a building exit, cellar access hatch, or areaway. The stated exception allows a platform over a cellar entrance or areaway only upon special application and commissioner permission, if it is easily removable, prominently designated, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, and the entrance or areaway is not used as a required means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility applies to the café and its access
supportedPoints.explanation: Sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces for food or drink are provided, at least 10 percent of total seating and standing spaces must be accessible, with at least one accessible dining surface of each type. Accessible dining surfaces must be distributed throughout the facility and be on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.heading: Enclosed café seating generally combines with interior seating
supportedPoints.explanation: For an enclosed sidewalk café, café seating must be added to seating inside the building to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless the areas are separated by fire partitions complying with Section 713.
